title: EXP-014 reduce Jolt no-libffi startup on tpb32l
description:
After the word-size patch mints a genuine tpb32l Jolt boot, the native target advances past hash/HAMT startup and aborts in Chez foreign-procedure with `protocol not supported (libffi unavailable)`, exit 134. Identify the first eager signature and determine a sustainable capability-aware Jolt correction compatible with the measured Emscripten static-FFI boundary. Do not no-op FFI, assume browser libffi, or weaken Jolt threads.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `nix develop -c ./experiments/EXP-014-jolt-tpb32l-emscripten/commands.sh host64-pack`, then `nix develop -c ./experiments/EXP-014-jolt-tpb32l-emscripten/commands.sh jolt-mint`. The mint succeeds; the scripted native probe retains the expected exit-134 no-libffi failure.
acceptance_criteria: Retain the exact first failing signature/site and no-patch log; distinguish guarded optional host facilities from required Jolt FFI; implement or propose the smallest semantic correction; prove unchanged app.witness reaches its Jolt startup/completion tokens under threaded Node Wasm or retain the next independently reduced blocker. Preserve EXP-006 ABI limits.
notes: T3 continuation proved 2026-08-31: static libffi 3.5.2 built with Emscripten 6.0.8-git; patched Chez configured --emscripten --threads --pbarch --enable-libffi; unchanged app.witness invoked via app.exp014 minted genuine tpb32l boot and Node output matched native expected exactly, including EXP-014-JOLT-COMPLETE, exit 0. Next dependency is browser T4/T5.
close_reason: No-libffi blocker resolved; canonical Jolt fixture runs under threaded Node Wasm with exit 0.

title: Review racket-wasm-backend as reference project
description:
Review bradlord/racket-wasm-backend at an exact revision for techniques relevant to Jolt/Chez tpb32l browser work. Distinguish transferable evidence from Racket-specific architecture and add a concise notice under this repository's related/reference projects.

## Steps to Reproduce

Inspect README.md, build-wasm.md, upstream lock, core patches, worker/runtime glue, and build/link configuration from a recorded Git revision.
acceptance_criteria: README related-projects notice links the project and succinctly states what it proves, which techniques are worth following here, and which differences prevent direct reuse. Exact reviewed revision and source-backed claims are retained in Beads notes; documentation passes markdown/diff checks.
notes: Reviewed bradlord/racket-wasm-backend commit 411393882a1e9d726edc5dbc230b24f96d335398 (2026-07-02), which pins upstream Racket 6917300ab79704436422d78cb00956d957092d0b. Source-backed transferable lead: it builds static libffi 3.5.2 (tarball sha256 f3a3082a23b37c293a4fcd1053147b371f2ff91fa7ea1b2a52e335676bac82dc) with emconfigure/-pthread, configures Chez --emscripten --pbarch --threads --enable-libffi, exports addFunction/removeFunction with a growable function table, registers static C symbols with Sforeign_symbol, and routes static lookup in lieu of dlopen. Racket upstream baseline c/ffi.c, c/foreign.c, s/pb.ss, and s/prims.ss are byte-identical to this project pinned Chez 7fadeee; its five Chez deltas (ffi.c, foreign.c, configure, pb.ss, prims.ss) all patch --dry-run cleanly with -p4 against the project source. Caveats: Racket-specific boot/rktio glue is not reusable as Jolt proof; browser build uses PROXY_TO_PTHREAD + pool 4, excluded from EXP-014; it disables places because FFI/WASMFS JS state in extra pthread workers is not shared. pbchunk is a later startup optimization, trading ~26 MB wasm + ~87 MB data for ~2 s boot. README related-project notice links the exact reviewed commit and states the useful boundary.
close_reason: Reviewed exact upstream implementation and added an evidence-bounded related-project notice with the directly applicable libffi/Chez lead and threading caveats.
